title: Nextech Alternative for Wellness and Aesthetic Clinics
summary: Looking for a Nextech alternative? See where cash-pay wellness and aesthetic clinics outgrow it, plus a 7-step demo checklist before you switch.
body_markdown:
## What Nextech Is Built For


Nextech is a specialty software company, and its strongest fit is a medical specialty practice that wants one vendor for clinical and business operations.[Its homepage](https://www.nextech.com/) lists five specialties (ophthalmology, plastic surgery, dermatology, med spa and orthopedics) and a product line that includes practice management, an EHR, payments, a CRM and revenue cycle services.


That is a sensible product for a surgical or dermatology group that bills insurance and needs specialty workflows. A clinic that sells weight loss programs, testosterone, peptides and memberships for cash is solving another problem, and the mismatch tends to appear in a handful of places.


## Where Wellness and Aesthetic Clinics Outgrow Nextech


Clinics outgrow Nextech when the business moves from episodic procedures to recurring programs. These are the situations operators described.


### Memberships the patient can actually see


The owner above wanted a membership model where the portal shows status, balance and expiry. Patients who cannot see what they have left call the front desk, and staff end up answering the same question by phone. Ask any vendor to enroll a test patient and show you the member's view, not the admin view. Our guide to[med spa membership pricing and retention](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-membership-pricing-retention) explains how to structure the plans themselves.


### Prescribing, including controlled substances


A clinic prescribing testosterone or other scheduled drugs needs electronic prescribing that meets the DEA's requirements for controlled substances.[21 CFR Part 1311](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-II/part-1311) is the rule to hand your vendor. The practical gap is often that prescribing lives in a separate tool from the chart, so the provider re-enters the same patient context. Our breakdown of[EPCS and PDMP workflow](https://decodahealth.com/blog/epcs-pdmp-compounding-hormone-clinic-emr) lists what to test.


### Labs that return to the chart


Wellness practices order panels constantly and review them over time. If results arrive as PDFs in a separate portal, the provider has to open a second system before every follow-up. See[what to test in EMR lab integration](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-emr-lab-integration) before you sign.


### Calls and texts handled by a separate vendor


This owner was paying a separate vendor for patient calls and texts, and wanted that gone. Consolidating means moving the number, so ask early. The[number porting guide](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-number-porting-practice-management) covers timing.


### More than one location, more than one provider


Two clinics and three providers sounds small, but it still needs one calendar that shows everyone and a way to stop providers from double-booking. Check how the schedule looks with both locations on screen, because that view tells you more than a feature list.

## Who Should Not Leave Nextech


Keep Nextech if your practice is a dermatology, plastic surgery or ophthalmology group where insurance claims drive most revenue. The specialty workflows and revenue cycle services on its site are why those groups choose it, and a platform built for elective care will not replace them. A complaint that amounts to one renewal price is a negotiation, not a migration.


Move when the cash menu has become the business, meaning injectables, hormone programs, weight loss, IV and memberships. If you are still early in the search, our[integrative EMR evaluation checklist](https://decodahealth.com/blog/integrative-emr-evaluation-checklist) and the[best EMR for longevity clinics](https://decodahealth.com/blog/top-emr-longevity-clinics) cover the wider field.


## Planning the Cutover When a Contract Date Is Fixed


A hard contract end date shortens every step, so work backward from it. Start with a decision about what to migrate and what to leave behind. Cleaning up a messy structure before it moves is cheaper than copying it, and several clinics we have spoken with moved only patient charts and inventory on purpose, then rebuilt services and pricing fresh.


Next, list the tools that touch the old system: the phone line, the card terminals, the lab accounts, any outside prescribing or supplement service. Each one has an owner and a lead time. A late port request is the most common reason a go-live slips, so ask for the porting request on day one.


Finally, book staff training before the go-live week and give providers time to open the new templates. A front desk that has practiced one checkout with charted items already in the cart will be faster on day one than a team learning it with patients waiting. Ask each vendor what the dated plan looks like and who owns each task. Our[PatientNow alternative](https://decodahealth.com/blog/patientnow-alternative) and[DrChrono alternative](https://decodahealth.com/blog/drchrono-alternative) guides compare other exits, and the[Boulevard](https://decodahealth.com/blog/boulevard-software-alternatives) and[Zenoti](https://decodahealth.com/blog/zenoti-alternative-wellness-clinics) posts cover practices leaving scheduling-first tools.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing a Nextech Alternative


Match the software to the revenue. A specialty group living on insurance claims should stay put, and a clinic built on memberships, injectables, hormones and weight loss is better served by one platform for charting, ePrescribing, labs, billing and phones. ## Frequently Asked Questions


What is the best Nextech alternative for a wellness or aesthetic clinic?


The best fit depends on how the clinic earns revenue. Nextech lists ophthalmology, plastic surgery, dermatology, med spa and orthopedics as its specialties, so a clinic built around memberships, injectables, hormones and weight loss often wants a platform designed for elective care. Decoda Health combines scheduling, charting, labs, ePrescribing, payments and phones in one system for that kind of practice.


Why do clinics leave Nextech?


The reasons operators give us are fit, not outages. A practice that adds memberships, wellness services or a second location often finds the software feels heavy and that key features sit in separate products. Individual experiences vary, so list your own three biggest daily frustrations before you start comparing vendors.


Can I switch from Nextech without losing charts and patient photos?


You should be able to, but ask each vendor in writing what transfers and who does the work. Demographics, notes and photos usually move, while prepaid packages, membership balances and uploaded documents are the items most often dropped. Decoda Health runs the migration itself and finishes it in 3-4 weeks, guaranteed.


How long does it take to replace Nextech?


Plan on weeks, not days, because data mapping, training and a clean cutover all take time. Decoda Health guarantees a 3-4 week migration, and we have scheduled faster go-lives for practices with a hard contract end date. Ask any vendor for a dated plan that names who owns each step.


Does a Nextech alternative need ePrescribing for controlled substances?


If you prescribe testosterone or other scheduled drugs, yes. DEA rules in 21 CFR Part 1311 set the identity proofing and two-factor requirements for electronic controlled substance prescriptions, so confirm the vendor supports them. Decoda Health supports ePrescribing for controlled substances inside the same chart as labs and notes.


Can I keep my phone number and replace my separate phone system?


Usually yes, because business numbers can be ported to a new provider. Decoda Health ports the existing number during onboarding and includes texting and a softphone in its telephony module, so a separate patient communication tool may no longer be needed. Ask for the porting timeline in writing.
